title: Daily Data-Latency Hotspots
dataSources: Daily life scores (`lifescore:daily`), personal SLO status (`personalslo:status`), cross-signal correlations (`correlation:pair`), plus every other `index=personal` sourcetype as input.
app: The meta layer — correlating every `index=personal` feed (sleep, activity, mood, weather, spend, productivity, home telemetry) into daily life scores, personal SLOs, and cross-signal anomaly detection, all computed in Splunk.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=personalslo:status
| stats latest(freshness_min) as freshness_min by service
| where freshness_min>180
| sort - freshness_min
description: Flags services in your personal stack whose data is arriving too slowly to stay useful.
value: Late data is almost as bad as missing data when you rely on dashboards for a quick daily read.
implementation: Emit freshness-minutes metrics for each personal service; alert when freshness exceeds your tolerated threshold.
visualization: Table of services with current freshness in minutes.
grandmaExplanation: It ranks which parts of your personal dashboard are arriving too late to be very useful anymore.
